haiku-low.q1: After the MsgSvc transaction commits, the sender gets an ack through the GW containing msg_id and seq.
haiku-low.q2: Sender gets an error; nobody receives it, since no outbox row exists. Retry must reuse the same client-generated msg_id.
haiku-low.q3: After 30 seconds without a heartbeat (clients send one every 10 s), the presence key expires and the user counts as offline.
haiku-low.q4: G's 5 s timer expires with no ack, so G asks the push service to notify the user and leaves the mailbox entry in place.
haiku-low.q5: It is logged and dropped: no retry, and the mailbox entry stays untouched.
haiku-low.q6: Pull pending entries, fetch bodies by msg_id from the DB, send per conversation in ascending seq; clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
haiku-low.q7: The message and its outbox row commit in one transaction, so the fan-out still happens later even if the writer crashes after commit.
haiku-low.q8: An in-memory online map (user_id to gateway node, 30 s TTL); a clean disconnect deletes the key, otherwise TTL expiry removes it.
haiku-low.q9: Dispatcher writes the pending entry, routes via the online map to G's queue, G writes the socket; a client ack within 5 s confirms.
haiku-low.q10: Dispatcher writes it per recipient before any live attempt, as pointers only in the pending table; removed on client ack, or after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: It reads the user's pending-table entries, then fetches message bodies by msg_id from the DB, after presence is set.
haiku-low.q12: The unacked bus event is redelivered, so another fan-out instance redoes the whole member list; idempotent puts and client dedup make it safe.

sonnet.q1: Only after the MsgSvc transaction (message insert + obx row) commits. The ack through the GW carries {msg_id, seq}.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error. No one receives it (no obx row, nothing published). The retry must carry the same client-generated msg_id.
sonnet.q3: After 30 s of silence (presence key TTL 30 s; heartbeats every 10 s reset it) the key expires and they count as offline.
sonnet.q4: G asks the push service to send a push, and the mailbox (pending) entry is left in place (not deleted).
sonnet.q5: The failure is logged only. No retry, and the mailbox row is untouched.
sonnet.q6: Per conversation in ascending seq order. Duplicate msg_ids are dropped by the client; live messages arriving during reconnect are slotted in by seq.
sonnet.q7: The obx row is committed in the same transaction as the message, so the relay still publishes it after the crash. A client retry with the same msg_id gets the original stored msg_id/seq ack.
sonnet.q8: In the online map / presence cache, an in-memory KV (user_id -> gateway node, TTL 30 s). Without a clean disconnect, the key expires after 30 s of no heartbeats.
sonnet.q9: The dispatcher looks up the user's node in the online map, then sends it to that node's (G's) delivery queue. G writes it to the socket and starts a 5 s timer. The client's ack within 5 s confirms arrival.
sonnet.q10: In the inbox/pending (mailbox) table, holding pointers only (user_id, conv_id, seq, msg_id). The dispatcher writes an entry for each recipient before attempting live delivery. Entries are deleted on client ack, or expire after 30 days (the message stays in history).
sonnet.q11: It sets presence, pulls the user's entries from the pending table, fetches the bodies by msg_id from the DB, and sends them.
sonnet.q12: The bus event wasn't acked, so it is redelivered and another FO/dispatcher instance redoes the whole member list. This is safe because the inbox put is idempotent on (user_id, msg_id) and clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
